subject: how to compute exceedance probability for each location

messages.author: facf981883688355
messages.subject: how to compute exceedance probability for each location
parts:
I am working on under-nutrition and i need to compute 40% reduction in stunting based on 2025 WHO target threshold but not getting result across the state. i need help.
this was the code.

excprob <- sapply(m1$marginals.fitted.values[1],
                  FUN = function(marg){1-inla.pmarginal(q = 0.40, marginal = marg)})
head(excprob)
i got single result. does it have something to do with   index?
fitted.Predictor.00001
            0.01970223

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] how to compute exceedance probability for each location
parts:
I'm pretty sure marginals.fitted.value is a list, and then
marginals.fitted.values[1] is also a list (the sublist containing only
the first element of the list).
I think you intended

excprob <- sapply(m1$marginals.fitted.values,

For extra code safety, I would strongly recommend vapply instead of
sapply as well:
excprob <- vapply(m1$marginals.fitted.values,
